parts: Lesson 1: Early Childhood Care and Education: Meaning and Significance — Summary

Early childhood is the period from birth to six years. The National ECCE Policy, 2013 divides it into three sub-stages: conception to birth, birth to three years and three to six years. 'Care' means love and affection with a healthy, hygienic, protective and stimulating environment; 'education' is acquiring knowledge, skills, attitudes and values through exploration, experimentation, observation, participation and interaction. So ECCE means care (including health and nutrition) together with early learning opportunities for all young children, through play-based, developmentally appropriate activities.

The first six years are the formative years: growth and development are fastest in all domains. Neuroscience shows that by the age of six, 90% of brain development has taken place. Poor home and school environments, too little stimulation, inadequate nutrition and poor health care lead to developmental delays. Quality ECCE helps children gain age-appropriate knowledge and skills and adjust better to formal school, so it must reach all children, especially the disadvantaged.

The aim of ECCE is quality care and learning opportunities for every child's overall development during the formative years. It aims to: make children feel safe, secure, accepted and respected; give good, balanced nutrition; build healthy habits, hygiene and self-help skills; develop language, communication and expression; ensure physical and motor development; foster sensory and cognitive abilities through engaging activities; promote pro-social skills and emotional wellbeing; and prepare children for formal learning in school.

Health, nutrition and hygiene: prenatal and postnatal care of the mother (nutritious food, immunisation, check-ups, safe delivery) and for the child a balanced diet, protection from infection, timely immunisation and medical care.

Care and protection: a physically and emotionally safe, secure environment with warm, responsive interaction. Early stimulation: inputs through seeing, hearing, touching, smelling and tasting, especially in the first three years; it builds neural pathways in the brain. Early learning: play, concrete experiences, observation, manipulation and experimentation for children of three to six years.

Development takes place in interrelated domains: physical-motor (height, weight, bones, gross and fine muscles, eye-hand coordination), socio-emotional (social norms, relationships, managing feelings), cognitive (thinking, remembering, reasoning, deciding) and language (listening, speaking, reading, writing).

Developmental milestones are age-specific skills in each domain; a child who does not reach them at the expected time has a developmental delay (causes: heredity, complications in pregnancy or birth, illness, accidents). Early intervention means acting as early as possible on a child's developmental and learning needs. Regular health check-ups and records help early detection; for example, a child who does not respond when called may have a hearing difficulty. Delays not addressed in time may become permanent.

Pioneers: Gijubhai Badheka founded Bal Mandir, a preschool in Bhavnagar, Gujarat (1920); Tarabai Modak founded the Nutan Bal Shikshan Sangh in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1926; the Montessori Method of Maria Montessori supports natural development in a prepared environment. Gandhi, Tagore and Zakir Hussain wanted children taught in the mother tongue and linked to their culture and community. The ICDS scheme (1975) addresses the health, nutrition and development of children under six and of pregnant and lactating mothers. The National ECCE Policy, 2013 widened access. ECCE is also given by private nurseries, kindergartens and NGOs.

UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989); World Conference on Education for All, Jomtien, Thailand (1990): 'learning begins at birth'; World Education Forum, Dakar, Senegal (2000): Education For All goals; World Education Forum, Incheon, Republic of Korea (2015): Sustainable Development Goal 4 — by 2030 all girls and boys should have access to quality early childhood development, care and pre-primary education so that they are ready for primary education.
